query: What signals suggest an expense will be declined?

per_column.name: asset_form_factor
per_column.rationale: A useful categorical axis to group declines by asset type. Mostly grounded in ci/short_description, but the 'iPod touch / ISP Services' row is labeled cloud_service, an unwarranted read of the source text.

per_column.name: asset_vendor
per_column.rationale: Vendor extracted from ci/description gives a genuine grouping axis. Samples are sound (Dell, other); 'other' is a reasonable fallback for silent rows.

per_column.name: is_premium_or_nonstandard_asset
per_column.rationale: Non-standard/premium status is a plausible decline signal. Groundedness is moderate: the criterion is somewhat subjective and samples show only 'False', with no clear evidence for how 'true' is warranted, but no contradiction observed.

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: Travel-related flag is a reasonable expense-policy axis for declines. Sample values (all False for hardware/service items) are consistent with the source text.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Presence-of-source_id is a plausible provenance signal, but it is a near-mechanical restatement of an existing original column and thus low leverage. Sample groundedness is questionable: the RAM row has a processed_date yet has_source_id=False while the iPod row has_source_id=True with no visible source_id in the sample, so the mapping is not clearly derivable.

per_column.name: has_processed_date
per_column.rationale: Directly and correctly derived from the existing processed_date column (nan -> False). Perfectly grounded but largely redundant with an original column, limiting analytical leverage.

per_column.name: description_specificity
per_column.rationale: Specificity/vagueness of a description is a strong potential decline signal (vague requests get declined). Sample categorizations align well with the source text.

per_column.name: ci_identifier_quality
per_column.rationale: Quality of the CI identifier is a reasonable data-hygiene axis for declines. But 'Random Access Memory Component' and 'ISP Services' labeled 'named_model' are shaky reads; these are generic labels, not named models.

per_column.name: submitting_department
per_column.rationale: Department could be a useful grouping axis, but an original 'department' column already exists, making this largely redundant. Values appear invented/inconsistent: no department source is shown in samples, and assignments look arbitrary, suggesting fabrication rather than extraction.

judge.rationale: The set offers several genuinely useful axes for predicting declines: asset type/vendor, description specificity, CI identifier quality, travel and premium flags. Groundedness is generally acceptable, with values mostly derivable from ci/short_description/processed_date and reasonable fallbacks for silent rows. However, several columns show hallucination or redundancy issues: asset_form_factor and ci_identifier_quality mis-read some generic items, submitting_department appears fabricated and duplicates an existing column, and has_source_id/has_processed_date are near-mechanical restatements of original columns with limited leverage.
